About MEDGLOBE Initiative
Health Access for Every Community
A Nigerian non-profit of health professionals driving medication adherence, free medical outreaches, and community health education in underserved communities — reaching thousands across Imo State, Lagos, and Abuja.

Bassey Austin is a leader, writer, and speaker whose work sits at the intersection of public health, storytelling, and human development. As Director of Projects and Administrator at MEDGLOBE Initiative — a Nigerian non-profit dedicated to medication adherence, free medical outreaches, and health education in underserved communities — he brings strategic clarity and operational discipline to work that genuinely changes lives.

His books — Made for More and Random Thoughts — reflect a voice built to resonate: honest, purposeful, and grounded in real experience. On stage, he brings the same energy he brings to the field — direct, engaging, and always worth the room's attention. Whether coordinating a community health outreach, drafting a chapter, or addressing an audience, Bassey shows up with one conviction: people deserve more than ordinary.

World Health Day Outreach: Abuja & Lagos

📍 Abuja (IDP Camp Durumi) & Lagos (Ejigbo), Nigeria

A high-impact dual-city medical intervention delivering vital health access directly to vulnerable and displaced populations. At the Durumi IDP Camp in Abuja and Ejigbo community in Lagos, Bassey Austin coordinated multidisciplinary clinical teams providing free comprehensive medical consultations, diagnostic screenings for hypertension and diabetes, dedicated mental health awareness and one-on-one consultations, and preventive nutrition talks. Over 100 insecticide-treated bed nets were distributed alongside essential family hygiene kits.

Rural Medical Mission November 14, 2025

Imo State Rural Community Medical Outreach

📍 Ihodimeze Community, Ikeduru, Imo State, Nigeria

A grassroots clinical outreach prioritizing rural maternal, child, and geriatric health. The mission delivered tailored clinical screenings, chronic disease education, and therapeutic interventions focused on elderly residents, pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers, and children. Austin's operational oversight ensured efficient triage, extensive vitals assessments, and immediate access to professional medical care and free essential pharmaceuticals.

Services & Direct Interventions
50 LLINs Distributed Free Medications Dispensing Medical Consultations Vitals Checks: BMI, Blood Sugar, BP, Temp Malaria Health Education Mental Health & High Blood Pressure First Aid & Nutrition Support Priority Maternal & Child Care
Epidemic Prevention Mission April 25, 2026
317 Beneficiaries

World Malaria Day Multi-State Project

📍 Imo (Ngugo Obaire), Lagos (Eti-Osa) & FCT-Abuja (Lugbe)

A synchronized tri-location public health campaign staged across three major Nigerian regions for World Malaria Day. Designed to break transmission cycles and reduce severe malaria complications in hard-to-reach settlements, the initiative combined targeted vector-control education with rapid diagnostic evaluation, direct medication dispensing, and widespread net distribution to households most at risk.

Services & Direct Interventions
110 LLINs (Insecticide Nets) Distributed Malaria-Focused Health Education Free Medication Dispense Symptom Recognition Sessions Vector Control & Prevention Multi-State Coordination
Humanitarian Relief October 2025
100 People Reached

Toronto Thanksgiving Project 2025

📍 Ontario Streets, Toronto, Canada

Direct street-level outreach addressing food insecurity and homelessness in urban Ontario. Mobilizing community care and holiday warmth, Bassey Austin engaged out-of-home individuals facing systemic vulnerability, providing nutritious hot meals, basic hygiene supplies, and compassionate support on the streets of Ontario during Thanksgiving.

Focus & Support
100 Out-of-Home Individuals Supported Street-Level Direct Outreach Thanksgiving Nutrition & Care Essential Hygiene Aid Community Dignity & Compassion
Urban Community Relief October 2026
148 People Reached

Toronto Thanksgiving Project 2026

📍 Etobicoke, Ontario, Canada

A scaled humanitarian follow-up expanding outreach across the Etobicoke district of Ontario. Reaching 148 vulnerable, displaced, and unhoused individuals with warm holiday meals, protective comfort packages, and person-centered support — cementing an enduring cross-border ethos of civic service and radical community care.
